stories.title: Atari puts Crossy Road co-creator Matt Hall in charge of its mobile games division
paragraphs: Atari named Matt Hall, co-founder of Hipster Whale and co-creator of Crossy Road, executive vice president of mobile, according to Game Developer and VGC.
The appointment puts a developer associated with a major mobile hit in charge of Atari's mobile division. The saved reports do not describe specific upcoming games or changes to Crossy Road.

scoreNotes.general: A notable leadership appointment links a globally recognized mobile-game creator with Atari's mobile strategy.
scoreNotes.heat: The appointment drew coverage from game-industry outlets, though the saved results contain no audience or market-response figures.
scoreNotes.time: Game Developer's report is dated October 27, inside this collection window.
scoreNotes.ethos: Game Developer and VGC report the appointment; the saved results do not give a detailed roadmap for the division.

stories.title: Sucker Punch cuts staff after Ghost of Yōtei as it plans its next project
paragraphs: Sucker Punch Productions has reduced its staff after releasing Ghost of Yōtei. Game Developer reports that an email to staff attributed the cuts to market challenges and the studio's needs for its next project.
Game Developer reports 24 jobs affected, while Gematsu reports 26. The saved reporting does not resolve the discrepancy or establish that the cuts signal a wider Sony restructuring.

scoreNotes.general: Job cuts at a prominent Sony studio are consequential for staff and raise questions about production after a major release.
scoreNotes.heat: The report prompted visible gaming-community discussion, while the saved results do not establish wider industry effects.
scoreNotes.time: A newer Game Developer report appeared October 27 after the initial October 26 report.
scoreNotes.ethos: Game Developer reports an employee email and says 24 jobs were cut; Gematsu reports 26, so the total is unresolved in the saved results.

citations.title: Sucker Punch lays off 24 to align with next project's needs
Report: Sucker Punch Productions lays off 26 staff

stories.title: Epic plans to let AI systems train on outputs from Unreal Engine and MetaHuman
paragraphs: Epic is changing its EULA to remove restrictions on training AI systems with outputs made using Unreal Engine and MetaHuman, Game Developer reports, citing CEO Tim Sweeney's post.
The report describes a planned license change, not a complete final set of terms. The saved evidence does not specify when the revised EULA will take effect or how Epic will define covered outputs.

scoreNotes.general: A proposed license change could affect how developers' work made with two widely used creation tools may be used for AI training.
scoreNotes.heat: The policy touches a consequential debate about creator control and AI, but the saved evidence does not measure developer reaction.
scoreNotes.time: Game Developer reports the proposed change on October 27.
scoreNotes.ethos: The report attributes the plan to Epic CEO Tim Sweeney; exact revised license language and implementation timing were not available in the saved results.

citations.title: Epic Games is updating its EULA to allow AI training

stories.title: Pokémon UNITE is scheduled to shut down in March 2027
paragraphs: The official Pokémon UNITE notice says the game's service will end on March 23, 2027 at 00:00 UTC.

The saved search results also surfaced matching notices on Pokémon's Japanese and Korean sites. The English notice returned an internal error when opened, and the saved evidence does not explain the decision or describe what happens to purchases before shutdown.

scoreNotes.general: Ending a live Pokémon game is a major decision for its players and a meaningful signal about the title's future.
scoreNotes.heat: The shutdown announcement surfaced across official regional results and game coverage, though the saved records contain no player-count or community-response measure.
scoreNotes.time: The notice appeared in this run's current searches, but its publication date was not visible and the official page failed to open.
scoreNotes.ethos: The official search result states the service-end date; the underlying notice could not be inspected, so further shutdown details are not included.

stories.title: Instagram tests a 90-minute widescreen video format called Features
paragraphs: Instagram is testing 'Features,' a horizontal video format that can run up to 90 minutes, according to Android Central and TechRepublic.

Instagram head Adam Mosseri and product chief Tessa Lyons discussed the test, which moves beyond the short vertical format associated with Reels. The saved reports do not establish when the feature will reach all users or whether it will include a creator ad-revenue share.

scoreNotes.general: The test pushes Instagram toward longer creator programming and a more direct competition with YouTube.
scoreNotes.heat: The format is strategically relevant to video creators, though the saved evidence gives no creator adoption or audience data.
scoreNotes.time: The test was announced October 26, shortly before this 24-hour window began, and is included as a new-to-Owl seven-day fallback story.
scoreNotes.ethos: Android Central and TechRepublic describe the test and its 90-minute horizontal format; broad availability and monetization terms remain unclear.

citations.title: Instagram wants in on 'long-form,' widescreen videos and its test begins now
